cm_hint_balanced: Balanced threshold (θ ≈ 0.50): Balanced precision ({$a->precval}%) and recall ({$a->recval}%).
cm_scenarios_medical_hint_high: Too high threshold: Sick patients are missed (unacceptable False Negatives)!
cm_scenarios_medical_hint_low: In medical screening, lower threshold is preferred to minimize deadly False Negatives (FN).
cm_scenarios_quality_hint_high: High threshold: High precision, but dangerous defective parts leak to customers (FN)!
cm_scenarios_quality_hint_low: Low threshold: High recall on defects, but more false alarms on good parts.
cm_scenarios_spam_hint_high: Conservative filter: Very few false positives, legitimate emails are safe.
cm_scenarios_spam_hint_low: Too aggressive: Important legitimate emails end up in spam.
conv_advice_abs: Edges also give negative values (light→dark), which show as black. Turn on the absolute value.
conv_advice_bright: The sum of the weights divided by the divisor is not 1, so the overall brightness changes.
conv_advice_close: Close! Check the signs of the weights, the divisor and the absolute value.
conv_advice_far: The output does not look like the target yet. What does the target show: edges, blur or sharpness?
conv_advice_free: Pick a ready-made filter or type your own weights. Every output pixel is the sum of the 9 surrounding pixels multiplied by the kernel weights.
conv_advice_solved: Well done! Your filter produces the target image.
conv_calc_hint: Tap a pixel on the input image or the output.
cv_advice_best: This degree has the lowest mean validation error (★). Now unlock the test set to see how good the chosen model really is.
cv_advice_fewfolds: With 2 folds every model learns from only half of the data, and the result jumps with every new split (🎲). Use more folds for a steadier estimate.
cv_advice_over: The training error is small, but the validation error has grown: the model learns the noise of the training points (overfitting).
cv_advice_start: Move the degree and compare the two curves: the training error always falls, the validation error does not.
cv_advice_tested: The test set has been used. If you change the degree now because of the test result, the test is no longer an honest measure – it has become a second validation set.
cv_advice_under: Degree too low: the model is too simple, so both the training and the validation error are high (underfitting).
cv_data_title: Data and the model trained on all training data
cv_degree_hint: The degree is a hyperparameter: the model does not learn it from the data, you choose it.
cv_folds_hint: The training data is split into k folds. Each fold is held out once, and the model trained on the other folds is measured on it.
db_advice_bias: The model fails for factory B because the sample hardly contains its parts – and a test set from the same sample does not reveal it. Increase the share of factory B.
db_advice_fair: Well done! The model works equally well for both factories.
db_advice_memorize: With k = 1 the model memorises every point: 100% on training means nothing. Look at the test set.
db_advice_small_test: The test set is very small: its accuracy jumps with every new sample.
db_advice_start: Move the share of factory B and compare the test-set accuracy with the real-world accuracy per factory.
db_legend: Filled mark = training, hollow = test. Red = defective, blue = good. Dashed line = the true rule, background = the model's decision.
db_share: Share of factory B in the sample
db_story: A model (k-NN) decides from two sensor readings whether a part is good or defective. Parts come from two factories: ● A (old line) and ■ B (new line), where the rule is slightly different.
dp_advice_drop: Dropping rows with missing values throws away data – and here the missing values are more common in one class, so that class loses examples.
dp_advice_good: A good pipeline: the data is clean and scaled, so every variable counts. The same steps, with the values learned on the training data, must be used for every new example.
dp_advice_outliers: Min-max scaling squeezes all normal values into a narrow band because of a few extreme values (look at the maximum in the table). Remove the outliers, or use z-score scaling.
dp_advice_scale: Without scaling, the variable with large numbers decides the distances, and the useful one is almost invisible – look at the view below: the points lie on a flat line. Choose a scaling.
dp_advice_start: Look at the statistics and the histograms first: what is wrong with this data? Then build the pipeline step by step.
dp_advice_zero: Replacing missing values with 0 invents measurements that never happened: look how the minimum and the mean change. A mean or a median is a more honest estimate.
dp_space_hint: Both axes have the same scale, because k-NN measures plain distances: a variable with large numbers decides almost alone.
gd_status_diverging: ⚠ Warning: Divergence! Learning rate too high.
gd_status_ready: Ready. Click Run, Step, or click curve to set w₀.
km_add_point_notice: Unsupervised: points have no labels. Click canvas to add custom points.
km_advice_elbow: Optimal K: The "elbow" marks the point of diminishing returns.
km_advice_high_k: K is too large: Natural clusters are fragmented artificially.
km_advice_low_k: K is too small: Natural groups are merged together.
knn_add_point_hint: Click canvas to add data points for active class.
knn_depth_hint: Depth 1 = single cut. Depth 4-5 creates fine rectangular boxes (overfitting).
knn_k_hint: k=1 creates jagged Voronoi cells (noisy). Larger k smooths boundary.
knn_knn_notice: k-NN creates smooth or jagged boundaries based on Euclidean distance.
knn_tree_notice: Decision Tree splits space with orthogonal axis-aligned cuts.
log_advice_good: The straight boundary separates the classes well. Now move the threshold θ and watch precision and recall change.
log_advice_ring: Logistic regression always draws a straight boundary, so it cannot separate a ring. That needs new features (such as x₁² + x₂²) or a neural network.
log_advice_start: Move the weights by hand, or press Train and watch gradient descent turn the boundary toward the data. Points with a black ring are misclassified.
log_advice_threshold: A high θ predicts class 1 only when the model is sure: precision goes up, recall goes down. A low θ catches more cases but raises more false alarms.
log_calc_hint: Tap a point on the map to see how the model computes its probability.
log_datasets_ring: 🎯 Part within tolerance (deviation in x and y)
log_threshold_hint: The model predicts class 1 when the probability σ(z) ≥ θ. A higher θ means fewer but surer alarms.
nn_advice_diverged: The loss exploded – the learning rate is too high. Lower it and create new weights.
nn_advice_perceptron: A perceptron (no hidden layer) can only draw a straight line. This data is not linearly separable – add a hidden layer.
nn_advice_solved: Well done! The network has learned to separate the classes.
nn_advice_start: Press “Train” and watch the network move its decision boundary.
nn_advice_stuck: Training has stalled. Try more neurons, another activation or new initial weights.
privacy:metadata: The AI Simulations Viewer filter does not store any personal data.
ql_advice_explore: The agent has not found the goal yet. Without exploration (ε) it repeats the same moves – raise ε or train longer.
ql_advice_longer: The agent reaches the goal, but not by the shortest path. Train more or lower ε.
ql_advice_solved: Well done! The learned policy takes the shortest path to the goal.
ql_advice_start: Press “Train”. The agent starts knowing nothing and learns from the reward after every move.
ql_advice_treasure: The agent takes the small nearby treasure because future rewards are worth little to it. Increase γ.
ql_advice_treasure_explore: The agent settled for the small treasure because it has not discovered the big one. Raise ε or start over.
ql_cell_hint: Tap a cell to see its Q-values.
ql_gamma: Discount factor γ (value of the future)
ql_legend: S start · G goal (+10) · T small treasure (+3) · red: cliff (−10) · every step −0.1. Cell colour = highest Q-value, arrow = best move.
reg_optimal: Good Fit: Optimal generalization to unseen data.
reg_overfitting: Overfitting: Model memorized noise instead of signal (High Variance)!
reg_reg_hint: L2 (Ridge) penalizes large weights, smoothing out overfitting.
reg_underfitting: Underfitting: Model is too simple (High Bias).
